deep.reconstruction:
This page is the plan for §4.2–4.3 of the 'laïus' that became Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES lectures, Dec. 1966; published in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968). The previous page reinterpreted a relative stratification of a module F on X/S. Such a stratification amounts to a compatible system of extensions of f^*F to infinitesimal thickenings Y' of S-schemes Y → X, whenever f extends (locally) to Y' → X. This extension condition is automatic when X/S is formally smooth. To make this systematic, Grothendieck introduces two sites.

(i) The crystalline site of X/S, which in characteristic 0 amounts to the infinitesimal site. Its objects are thickenings U ↪ T over S, with U open in X (in the variant, U → X arbitrary), and nilpotent ideal (with PD structure in the later p-adic version).

(ii) The stratifying site, which in Berthelot's later terminology is the variant where U → X need not be an open immersion.

The remark 'C'est pareil si X formellement lisse sur S' says that for X/S formally smooth the two points of view give equivalent topoi, or at least equivalent categories of crystals.

The warning 'Attention, les sites n'ont pas en général d'objet final !' notes a known subtlety. Global sections, and hence cohomology, are not evaluations at a final object. They are computed as Hom(e, -), or as a limit over the site, which is why cohomology is defined via the topos.

The ringed-topos case is set up with the structure ring O. Sheaves of sets, rings and modules are described 'in terms of usual sheaves': a sheaf is a family of Zariski sheaves F_T on each thickening T, with transition maps u^{-1}F_T → F_{T'} for morphisms T' → T, satisfying cocycle conditions.

'Faisceaux spéciaux' are those whose base-change maps u^*F_T → F_{T'} are isomorphisms; these are crystals. He then states the equivalence: special sheaves of modules on the stratifying site of X/S ≃ O_X-modules with stratification relative to S.

§4.3 announces results to be detailed later. Theorem: if S has characteristic 0 and X is smooth over S, then H^*_cris/strat(X/S, O) ≅ H^*_DR(X/S). A struck-out relative version reads Rf_{cris*}(O) ≅ Rf_*(Ω^•_{X/S}).

The next page states the conjecture H^*_inf(X/C) ≅ H^*(X^an, C) for arbitrary X locally of finite type over C. It is proved in the smooth case by combining this theorem with the analytic comparison theorem. The point is that this gives a description of de Rham cohomology 'without differentials'.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalence 'special modules on the stratifying site ≃ stratified modules' and the identity of crystalline and stratifying descriptions need care without formal smoothness. Grothendieck flags this himself ('C'est pareil si X formel. lisse sur S').
The struck-out relative statement was abandoned on the page; its final form appears in Crystals §4 as the comparison of Rf_{inf*} with the de Rham complex.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a lecture outline whose content appears essentially verbatim in the published 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'. It is of historical interest as a draft only.
transcription_corrections: The line read as 'Cas [?] des topos annelés' is 'Ce cas des topos annelés'. It is a first attempt, rewritten below as 'Cas des [sites] et topos annelés' with 'annelés' underlined.
'Attention, les sites n'ont pas en général d'objet final !' is underlined.
'(lisse car)' is more plausibly '(lisse cas)' or the start of an abandoned clause leading into the crossed-out relative statement.
Crossed-out formula: likely '(R f_{cris*}(O_X))^{an} ≃ R f_*(Ω^•_{X/S})', the relative version. The superscript is uncertain ('sub' in the machine transcription).
Under H^* the subscript reads 'cris/strat' (or 'strat'), i.e. cohomology of either the crystalline or stratifying topos.
